description:
## Why

S/MIME-in-production bar requires the smime crate not error on valid messages in the wild. Real-world S/MIME corpus has a long tail of certs from older issuance:

* **RSA-PKCS1v15 + SHA-1** (`1.2.840.113549.1.1.5`) — used by older government PKI (DoD pre-~2018, federal bridge cross-certs), legacy commercial CAs, many self-managed enterprise CAs.
* **ECDSA + SHA-1** (`1.2.840.10045.4.1`) — rarer but exists in older deployments.

Without these verifiers, `pkix-path` rejects these chains as `AlgorithmNotAllowed` (or `signature::Error` from `DefaultVerifier` with no detail). The smime crate has no way to validate the chain and decide policy ('verify but warn user' is the standard browser/mail-client behaviour). CA/B Forum S/MIME BR forbids new SHA-1 issuance, but messages signed years ago sit in mailboxes for decades and the smime crate must still verify them.

## What

In `pkix-path/src/lib.rs`, two new unit-struct verifiers under separate feature flags so security-conscious downstream consumers can compile them out:

1. `RsaPkcs1v15Sha1Verifier` behind `feature = "rsa-sha1"`. Mirror `RsaPkcs1v15Sha256Verifier` at `lib.rs:1909`. Reuse `sha1` workspace dep (already present per `Cargo.toml:52`).
2. `EcdsaP256Sha1Verifier` behind `feature = "ecdsa-sha1"`. Mirror `EcdsaP256Verifier` at `lib.rs:1867`. Note: ECDSA-SHA1 covers all curves; for the verifier impl this is P-256 + SHA-1. P-384/P-521 + SHA-1 combinations exist in the wild but are extraordinarily rare; document as out-of-scope.

OID dispatch in `DefaultVerifier` (`lib.rs:3047`) for both, gated by `#[cfg(feature = ...)]`.

## Security framing (rustdoc must call this out)

`# Security` section on each verifier explaining:

* SHA-1 collision attacks are practical (SHAttered, 2017). A SHA-1-signed cert can be substituted by an attacker with sufficient resources.
* These verifiers are provided **for legacy interop only**. New deployments MUST NOT use them.
* The default feature set (`rustcrypto`) MUST NOT include `rsa-sha1` or `ecdsa-sha1`. Consumers opt in explicitly.
* Recommend smime/cms callers gate SHA-1 acceptance behind a separate runtime policy flag (e.g. "accept legacy SHA-1 with prominent warning") rather than always-accept.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `RsaPkcs1v15Sha1Verifier` and `EcdsaP256Sha1Verifier` compile cleanly with their feature flags enabled.
- [ ] Default workspace build (no `rsa-sha1` / `ecdsa-sha1`) does NOT include them — confirm via `cargo hack check --feature-powerset --depth 2`.
- [ ] Unit tests verify a known-good SHA-1 signature using independent test vectors (RustCrypto `rsa` or `ecdsa` crate test vectors).
- [ ] Tampered-signature test rejects.
- [ ] `DefaultVerifier` dispatches when feature enabled; returns `signature::Error` when disabled.
- [ ] Real-world legacy S/MIME chain added to `pkix-difftest/tests/fixtures/` (e.g. extract a SHA-1 cert from any older corpus). Smoke-test that with the feature on, validation succeeds.
- [ ] `# Security` rustdoc block on each verifier with collision-attack note.
- [ ] Top-level `pkix-path` README and `# Limitations` section updated to note these are available but not in the default crypto set.

## Out of scope

- ECDSA-SHA1 for curves other than P-256.
- SHA-1 in TLS (this is for cert validation; TLS handshake hash is a TLS concern).
- MD5-based signatures (id-md5WithRSAEncryption, etc.) — refuse to implement; collision attacks have been practical since 2008. If a downstream consumer needs MD5 they can implement `SignatureVerifier` themselves and accept the security cost.

## Filed as

PKIX-gphz child #6, P2 under the S/MIME-in-production bar. Not on my original v1.0 bar list — surfaced when user articulated the smime-bar-must-not-error standard.
title: crypto: legacy SHA-1 SignatureVerifiers (RSA + ECDSA, feature-gated, off by default)
